task: PR #1173 scope note: _incremental_sync (engine.py:149) still re-lexes the entire current prefix on every call (proposed_fix_sketch item 2 from decode-compiler-tree-lexer-rebuild-cost-finding.json, not applied in PR #1173). Measure the real wall-time cost at realistic prefix lengths and apply the fix if warranted.

measured_before_fix.interpretation: near-constant sync_ms/chars^2 across a >10x length range is the signature of O(n^2) whole-session cost; root cause confirmed by reading _incremental_sync: it already tracks _fed_token_count for feeding but calls _lex_tokens(prefix) with the FULL prefix on every call before slicing, so no lexing work was ever actually saved.

summary: New self._settle_pos: int -- character offset of the start of the last fed token; every token strictly before it is provably final (openui.lark has no lookbehind/word-boundary regex assertions, verified via grep). Initialized to 0 in __init__ and reset().
New _update_settle_pos(tokens, token_index_offset=0) helper updates _settle_pos after any successful sync.

_incremental_sync now lexes only prefix[self._settle_pos:] (the 'unsettled tail') instead of the whole prefix; tail token start_pos values are offset back to absolute coordinates. The existing shrink/identity-mismatch guard (NAME/COMPONENT gluing) is preserved, computed against the smaller tail_tokens list spliced onto self._fed_tokens[:prev_settled_count]; any divergence still falls back to _full_sync(prefix), same safety net as before.
fix.why_safe: openui.lark (75 lines) has no lookbehind/word-boundary assertions (grep -nE '\\b|\(\?<|\(\?!|\(\?=' -> no matches). Lark's BasicLexer is a stateless regex-based longest-match-with-priority scanner: a token's end boundary is decided purely from characters up to that boundary. Every token before the last fed one stopped because of a mismatching character already present in the previously-synced prefix -- appending more text cannot retroactively change that. Only the last fed token could have stopped solely because the prefix ran out, so it is the only one that can still grow. Re-lexing prefix[_settle_pos:] as a standalone substring reproduces what a full lex would give for that region since nothing before it participates in matching decisions at/after it.

interpretation: Closes proposed_fix_sketch item 2 from decode-compiler-tree-lexer-rebuild-cost-finding.json and the explicit open question in PR #1173's scope note. _incremental_sync re-lexed the whole prefix on every call even after PR #1173's lexer-construction cache -- only the lexer OBJECT was reused, the lexing WORK was not made incremental. This made a growing decode session's total lex cost O(n^2) (81.2x amplification on a realistic 326-char record). The fix exploits the grammar's lack of lookbehind to prove only the last fed token can still be open, reducing re-lex scope to the unsettled tail and restoring O(n) session cost, with a speedup that grows with prefix length (2.6x->14.4x across 326-3580 chars) rather than PR #1173's flat ~2x per-call constant-cost removal.
